MOTOR CARRIER TERMINAL AREAS AND OPERATING RIGHTS:
At Municipalities: Section 202(c) allows motor carriers to conduct, either directly or by contract with others, exempt collection and delivery if it is "incidental to" motor carrier linehaul service and "within terminal areas." Consequently, both section 202(c) and 203(b)(8) express their respective exemptions in geographic terms, although the geographic limits of these exemptions are not specified in the Act. In 1952, the Commission concluded that the geographic limits of a motor carrier's terminal area at a particular municipality should be equated to the commercial zone limits of that municipality, Commercial Zones, 54 M.C.C. 21, 109 (1952). This rule of coextensive limits was not mandated by statute but was based upon our interpretation of the reasonable limits of terminal areas within the meaning of section 202(c). It has also been noted that such a rule "achieves a desirable uniformity and ... contribute(s) in no small way to the simplification of regulation benefiting both carriers and public." Commercial Zones, 48 M.C.C. at 433.
